title: Juniper Green Energy IPO Closes 8x Oversubscribed as Institutions Drive Final-Day Surge
excerpt: The ₹1,800 crore renewable energy IPO saw QIB demand reach 26x on its last day, though retail investors stayed cautious at just 0.68x subscription.
body:
• Juniper Green Energy's ₹1,800 crore IPO closed with 8.22x overall subscription on August 3, driven by qualified institutional buyers at 26.22x
  • Retail investor participation remained below par at 0.68x, while non-institutional investors subscribed 1.86x
  • The company, backed by Singapore's AT Capital Group, operates solar, wind, hybrid, and battery storage projects across India

Juniper Green Energy's initial public offering closed on August 3 with an overall subscription of 8.22 times, powered by a massive final-day rush from institutional investors. The ₹1,800 crore offering, priced at ₹214-225 per share, saw qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) subscribe 26.22 times their allotted portion on the last day alone, up sharply from 1.25x at the end of Day 2.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed 1.86 times their quota, crossing the 1x mark on the final day. Retail investors, however, remained underwhelming at 0.68x — failing to fully subscribe their reserved portion.

From Tepid to Oversubscribed in Three Days

The IPO had a slow start. On Day 1 (July 30), overall subscription stood at just 0.38x, with retail at 0.13x and NIIs at a mere 0.05x. QIBs were the only category above 1x at 1.05x. By Day 2, the overall figure inched up to 0.49x. The transformation came on the final day, when institutional capital flooded in — QIB subscription jumped from 1.25x to 26.22x, dragging overall numbers past the 8x mark.

"The IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares with no offer-for-sale component."

— Red Herring Prospectus, Juniper Green Energy

Strong Anchor Book Sets the Tone

Ahead of the public issue, Juniper Green Energy raised ₹539.4 crore from 31 anchor investors on July 29, allotting 2.4 crore equity shares at ₹225 per share — the upper end of the price band. The anchor book featured heavyweight names: Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Nippon India Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Bajaj Life Insurance, Tata AIG General Insurance, and HDFC Life Insurance.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for 74.79 percent of the anchor portion, receiving 1.79 crore shares across 24 schemes from nine fund houses, according to a BSE circular.

The Company: India's Clean Energy Push

Juniper Green Energy, headquartered in Gurugram, develops, builds, and operates utility-scale solar, wind, hybrid, and battery energy storage projects. Backed by Singapore-based AT Capital Group, the company has built an integrated platform spanning project development, engineering, procurement, construction, and operations.

Its portfolio is concentrated in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh. The company has commissioned India's first merchant 100 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) in Rajasthan and begun phased commissioning of an integrated Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) project combining solar, wind, and battery storage.

At the upper price band, the post-issue market capitalization stands at approximately ₹12,802 crore. Promoter holding will dilute from 100 percent to 85.94 percent after the offering.

Use of Proceeds

The company plans to use ₹683.24 crore from IPO proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings. Another ₹728.69 crore will go to subsidiaries — Juniper Green Gamma One, Juniper Green Kite, and Juniper Green Power Five — to reduce their outstanding loans. The remainder is earmarked for general corporate purposes.

Muted GMP Signals Cautious Listing Expectations

The grey market premium (GMP) has been volatile. It stood at zero on July 27, rose to ₹8 by July 29, and has since settled at ₹2 per share post-subscription, according to IPO tracking platforms. That implies an estimated listing price of around ₹227 — a modest 0.89 percent premium over the upper band price of ₹225.

"QIB demand above 50x tends to support listing sentiment, as institutional investors are seen as informed buyers."

— IPOwiz analysis

Diaspora Angle

India's renewable energy sector continues to attract global capital, a trend underlined by the participation of Abu Dhabi Investment Authority in Juniper Green's anchor round. For NRI investors tracking India's energy transition, the IPO's institutional backing offers a signal — though the tepid retail response and low GMP suggest limited near-term listing upside. The company's BESS and hybrid projects position it in a segment that global clean-energy investors increasingly prioritize.

What's Next

Share allotment is expected on August 4, with refunds and demat credit scheduled for August 5. Juniper Green Energy shares are set to list on both BSE and NSE on August 6. ICICI Securities, HSBC Securities, JM Financial, and Kotak Mahindra Capital are the book-running lead managers, with KFin Technologies as registrar.

The minimum lot size is 66 shares, requiring a retail investment of ₹14,850 at the upper band. Eligible employees received a ₹21 per share discount.
nri_angle: India's renewable energy sector draws global capital including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority; NRI investors tracking India's clean energy transition will note the strong institutional backing despite muted retail participation.
author: Diaspora Desk
